text:
alice: Quick UX/prod question — when a saved query runs the platform can route to fallback model(s) if the primary is overloaded. Console list currently shows the saved query's configured model but not which fallback would be used. This causes confusion during rollouts and when cost/latency change. Should we surface the resolved fallback in the saved queries list?

ben: +1. Seen support tickets where token burn changed after a swap and users didn't know fallbacks differed (eg quant variant). Even a small badge would cut down noise.

olivia: Two big choices: snapshot the resolved model at save/preview time (stable but may become stale) or dynamically resolve on every render (always accurate but extra load / flakiness).

raj: From the routing API side we already have model_priority arrays per route. SavedQuery currently references route_id. Proposal: savedquery can optionally store a small "preview_models" list computed by routing-service, plus a timestamp. Console shows that preview and a refresh action.

carmen: UX idea: in the saved query row show compact line: "resolves to: gptx-1 → gptx-1-quant" with a tooltip showing median latency and cost delta and a tiny canary flag if one of the candidates is canary. Example: MyQuery • route /invoices • model gptx-1 (→ gptx-1-quant) • est +20ms, +$0.0002/token :money_with_wings: 

alice: API debate: should savedquery include a permanent "pinned_resolved_model" when user hits Save As Snapshot? That would preserve exact runtime behavior for reproducibility. Otherwise, users might save a query and later run it against a different resolved model without realizing.

ben: Operational note: dynamic resolves for the list view could increase calls to routing-service. We should avoid N+1 on page load. Cache previews in backend or return previews lazily via a batch endpoint.

olivia: UX compromise: show cached preview + a refresh icon. When user clicks refresh we call routing-service and update preview_models and preview_generated_at. Add hover copy: "Last resolved: 2025-03-10 14:10 UTC — click to refresh".

raj: Sketch of minimal API fields (informal):
```
SavedQuery {
  id: string,
  route_id: string,
  model_hint: string,         // user's preferred model
  preview_models: [string],   // resolved candidates by priority (optional)
  preview_generated_at: int,  // unix ts when preview was computed
  preview_ttl_seconds: int    // how long console should treat preview as fresh
}
```
This keeps the core contract small.

carmen: For console visuals: small pill with arrow "gptx-1 → gptx-1-quant" and color flags: green = same family, amber = different flavor/quant, red = different family. Tooltip includes cost/latency numbers and a link to "Why did this resolve?" that opens the route inspector.

alice: Also a data/export consideration: include preview_models and preview_generated_at in savedquery export so customers and audits can see what actually resolved at snapshot time.

ben: Telemetry: emit `savedquery.preview.refreshed` and `savedquery.run.resolved_model` events with routing_reason to measure confusion and divergence between preview and run-time resolution.

deploy-bot: routing-service v1.12 deployed — routing-preview endpoint enabled (batch /routing/preview) — 2025-03-10 14:23 UTC

olivia: Next steps: I'll make a compact mock (badge + tooltip) and a small PR for the API shape. Assigning: @olivia mockups, @raj API shape + routing-preview endpoint docs, @ben infra caching. I'll follow up with a quick proto for preview TTL defaults (suggest 5m).

carmen: +1, love the TTL default. Also think about an opt-out for orgs who don't want dynamic previews.

alice: Great — thanks all. If you can drop quick prototypes by EOD Friday we can include this in the next console minor release notes. :thumbsup:
